clue.text: Maybe double-decker dropping off one rider in Suffolk town for the beach? …

indicators.note: the town lets go of some of its letters, and 'for' brings in replacements in their place

parts.note: Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk, in eastern England
one as the Roman numeral I
a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript, abbreviated PS
a beach is made of sand

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in a Suffolk town watches a bus put down a passenger heading for the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IPS (I for one, PS for rider) out of IPSWICH and put SAND in its place, as 'for' says. The dots link this clue to the next two, which also use a double-decker bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-decker can be a sandwich with three slices of bread and two layers of filling, so it is an example.

clue.text: Away player might turn rude later

indicators.note: turning round signals the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A sports player on tour could become rude later in the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away player' looks like a visiting sportsman; it means someone who plays away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: To play away is slang for being unfaithful, so an adulterer is one who does that.

clue.text: Theatrical work about Greek nymph seen in museum display

explanation.definitionFit: To give way is to yield or surrender, a straight synonym of submitting.
